newsitem.title: USA: ATHLETICS-AUSTIN GUNNING FOR U.S. HIGH JUMP RECORD.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-AUSTIN GUNNING FOR U.S. HIGH JUMP RECORD.

text.p: Olympic high jump champion Charles Austin said Friday he expects to top his own American indoor record Saturday at the USA Indoor Track and Field Championships.
Austin, who claimed Olympic high jump gold last year and set the American indoor record at this meet a year ago, said his training has prepared him for strong showings in this year's major events.
"Hopefully, I'm looking at a record here and moving on to the world championships and winning that as well with a really high jump," Austin said.
Even a successful assault on his U.S. record of 2.32 meters, however, should leave the top American behind the eight-year-old world indoor mark of 2.43 meters held by Cuba's Javier Sotomayor.

Others competing in Saturday's indoor nationals said their primary goal was to earn a place on the U.S. team for the World Indoor Athletics Championships in Paris next month. To qualify they must finish first or second in their event final.
Sprinter Dennis Mitchell, who finished a disappointing fourth in the Olympic 100 meters, said he had been taking it easy so far this year.
"This indoor season has been relatively slow for me in comparison to other seasons because it was a very long and hard outdoor season for me last year," Mitchell said.
"I wanted to take things a little bit slower this year, and I have."

The meet also will feature the resumption of the sprint rivalry between women's Olympic 100 meters champion Gail Devers and Atlanta native Gwen Torrence. Last week, Devers again outran Torrence with a 7.07 clocking over 60 meters.
Mark Everett, who watched the Olympics on television after failing to make the American 800-meter team, said Friday he has adopted a take no prisoners attitude.
"It's time to take the records back," declared Everett.
Evert said he will set the pace and issued a warning to his competition.
"If anybody dares to get in front of me, they're going to get hurt."
